memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'then the person who brings an offering shall present to the Lord a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of olive oil. With each lamb for the burnt offering or the sacrifice, prepare a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering. With a ram prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil, and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering. Offer it as an aroma pleasing to the Lord.'" — Num 15:4-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses are full of measurements — flour, oil, wine, in careful proportions. It would be easy to skim past them as dry ritual detail. But there is beauty here if we look closely. God cared about the details of worship, and He was teaching His people that coming before Him was not a careless, casual thing.

Notice that every animal sacrifice was to be accompanied by grain, oil, and wine. The worshipper did not merely bring meat; they brought bread and drink as well — the fruits of their fields and labour. Worship engaged the whole of life. Everything they had, from flock to field to vineyard, was brought and offered to God.

This speaks to us about the wholeness of true worship. God does not want a slice of our lives while we keep the rest for ourselves. He is worthy of everything — our work, our resources, our daily bread, our joys. The careful completeness of these offerings pictures a heart that holds nothing back from God.

Under the new covenant, we no longer bring flour and wine to an altar. Instead, Paul urges us to offer our whole selves as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God. This is our true and proper worship. And we can do so freely because Christ has offered the one perfect sacrifice that these smaller offerings only pointed toward. Our worship now flows not from obligation but from gratitude — a whole life gladly given to the God who gave His Son for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you offer God a slice of your life or the whole of it?
2. What "fields and vineyards" of your life is God asking you to bring to Him?
3. How does Christ's perfect sacrifice free you to worship with gladness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are worthy of my whole life, not just a portion. Help me to offer everything I am and have as a living sacrifice of worship. Thank You that Christ's perfect offering makes my worship acceptable to You. Amen.
